assertions.name: bar_is_an_involution_on_every_basis_element
assertions.source: bar(bar(T_w)) = T_w for all six w - the map is an involution, so 'bar-odd' and 'bar-even' are well-defined eigenspaces

assertions.name: bar_is_independent_of_the_reduced_word
assertions.source: bar(T_0)bar(T_1)bar(T_0) = bar(T_1)bar(T_0)bar(T_1): the inverses satisfy the braid relation, so bar(T_w) is well-defined

assertions.name: neither_element_lies_in_the_two_row_quotient
assertions.source: chi^(1,1,1)(Delta_S) = (q - 1)*(q + 1)*(q**2 + 1)/(2*q**2) != 0 and chi^(1,1,1)(Delta_L) = -0.171538643777 != 0 - the element analogue of the admissible-root criterion selects NEITHER, so the criterion is about the functional alone

assertions.name: the_fork_survives_descent
assertions.source: Delta_S and Delta_L differ ALREADY in the two-row part (chi^(2,1) = 0 vs -0.106814457652), so no admissible functional identifies them: the fork cannot be deferred to the z-side

assertions.name: no_rescaling_identifies_the_two_models
assertions.source: chi^(2,1)(Delta_S) = 0 while chi^(2,1)(Delta_L) != 0, so no scalar multiple of one is the other - the fork is not a normalisation

assertions.name: net_equals_tr_at_z_one_ONLY_when_e_minus_vanishes
assertions.source: in GENERAL tr_M(z=1) - net = h * (e_minus coordinate), since tr_M(z=1) weights the basis [1,1,1,1,1,h+1] and net weights it [1,1,1,1,1,1]. Both Delta models have e_minus = 0, so they coincide HERE -- but the identity is not general and must not be quoted as one

assertions.name: short_model_is_exactly_bar_odd
assertions.source: bar(Delta_S) = -Delta_S identically in q. Term by term: bar(h) = -h so bar(h^2/2) = h^2/2 and bar(-h/2) = h/2, while bar(T_s) = T_s - h; the two h^2/2 contributions cancel to -h^2/2 and the generator terms flip sign

assertions.name: long_model_is_neither_bar_odd_nor_bar_even
assertions.source: bar(Delta_L) is neither -Delta_L nor +Delta_L - the 11-crossing word has no definite bar parity

assertions.name: long_model_has_a_nonzero_bar_even_part
assertions.source: Delta_L = (bar-odd part) + (bar-even part) with the even part nonzero; its counit is -0.0395652309646 - it is the even part that spoils the parity

assertions.name: long_models_bar_odd_part_is_not_the_short_model
assertions.source: the bar-odd part of Delta_L is NOT a scalar multiple of Delta_S - so the short model is not recoverable from the long one by projecting onto the bar-odd eigenspace

assertions.name: bar_reduces_the_symmetric_family_to_two_scalar_equations
assertions.source: on x = c + d(sigma_0+sigma_1), bar(x) = (cbar - 2h*dbar) + dbar*(sigma_0+sigma_1) - verified on a generic Laurent pair - so bar(x) = -x reduces to exactly two equations: dbar = -d, and c + cbar = -2hd

assertions.name: the_corpus_crossing_coefficient_is_bar_odd
assertions.source: d = -h/2 satisfies dbar = -d, so the corpus's 1-crossing coefficient already sits in the bar-odd eigenspace

assertions.name: bar_oddness_forces_the_bar_even_part_of_c_to_h2_over_2
assertions.source: with d = -h/2 the condition is c + cbar = h^2, so the BAR-EVEN part of c is forced to be exactly h^2/2 while its bar-odd part is free: adding the bar-odd h keeps the element bar-odd, adding the bar-even h^2 destroys it. h^2/2 is DERIVED from the involution, not fitted

assertions.name: the_forced_coefficient_is_the_one_the_ladder_uses
assertions.source: net(Delta_S) = h^2/2 - h = epsNPq, the counit the published ladder is built from - so the forced h^2/2 is not an incidental coefficient but the one the corpus consumes

assertions.name: the_two_models_are_separated_at_both_admissible_parameters
assertions.source: tr_M differs between the models at z = q AND at z = z_D, confirming from the functional side what chi^(2,1) shows from the block side: no admissible functional identifies them

description: qou-bg3w: the admissible-root criterion picks the FUNCTIONAL but not the ELEMENT (neither Delta has vanishing (1^3) component). A different canonical criterion -- the Kazhdan-Lusztig bar involution bar(q)=1/q, bar(T_s)=T_s^-1 -- DOES separate them: Delta_S is exactly bar-odd, identically in q; Delta_L is neither bar-odd nor bar-even. Scope-(a): a structural measurement, not an adjudication of the fork.
